cohort: 100 neonates, 50 born to mothers with hypothyroidism and 50 born to euthyroid mothers, excluding those with birth asphyxia, congenital anomalies, sepsis, metabolic disorders, or born to diabetic or anticonvulsant-using mothers.
finding: Neonates born to hypothyroid mothers had significantly higher rates of cesarean delivery, preterm deliveries, low birth weight, small for gestational age, and neonatal jaundice requiring phototherapy.
mod_finding: Neonates born to hypothyroid mothers had a significantly higher rate of cesarean delivery (LSCS) compared to controls.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was a measured outcome, and mean birth weight was significantly lower in the hypothyroid group.
gest_age: Preterm delivery and small for gestational age were measured outcomes, both significantly higher in the hypothyroid group.
